newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe says he'll quit whoever wins poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe says he'll quit whoever wins poll.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday he intends to resign from the premiership whoever wins next Sunday's parliamentary election runoff after the opposition left outpolled his centre-right coalition in the first round.
Juppe told a meeting of coalition leaders: "We need a new team led by a new prime minister."

The Gaullist premier has borne the brunt of blame from voters for austerity, high taxes and record unemployment in the two years since President Jacques Chirac took office and was widely held responsible for the conservatives' poor showing in Sunday's first round.
Juppe, 51, is Chirac's longest-serving political associate and aides told reporters only last week that the president hoped to reappoint him if the centre-right won the election.
His decision to sacrifice himself enables Chirac to promise voters a fresh start if they re-elect the coalition rather than forcing him to "cohabit" with a hostile, Socialist-led government.
